# Template errors and warnings

Diagnostics about T# templates: compile-time and run-time scopes, unsupported C# constructs, and template parameters.

| Article | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| <xref:lama0101> | A template uses a C# language feature that T# doesn't support. |
| <xref:lama0104> | A template expression is run-time where Metalama expects compile-time, or the opposite. |
| <xref:lama0105> | A local variable declaration in a template mixes compile-time and run-time variables. |
| <xref:lama0108> | A template sets a compile-time variable declared outside a block that depends on a run-time condition. |
| <xref:lama0109> | The template compiler can't find the declaration of a local symbol used in a template. |
| <xref:lama0110> | A template has a compile-time while or do loop in a block that depends on a run-time condition. |
| <xref:lama0113> | An aspect type of a referenced assembly can't be found in the current compilation. |
| <xref:lama0114> | A template references the current instance, but the advice is applied to a static member. |
| <xref:lama0115> | A template uses a meta.Target member that doesn't apply to the declaration the advice is applied to. |
| <xref:lama0117> | Code that isn't compile-time references a compile-time-only declaration. |
| <xref:lama0118> | Compile-time code was modified, and Metalama paused design-time analysis until the next build. |
| <xref:lama0119> | A file that contains compile-time code doesn't import a Metalama.Framework namespace. |
| <xref:lama0220> | A template references another template that isn't a method. |
| <xref:lama0221> | A template uses the this keyword where a run-time expression is expected. |
| <xref:lama0222> | The compile-time project, made of the aspects and other compile-time code, can't be compiled. |
| <xref:lama0223> | A template calls a Proceed variant that doesn't match the return type of the target method. |
| <xref:lama0224> | A template declares a dynamic local variable without initializing it. |
| <xref:lama0225> | A template initializes a dynamic local variable with null, default, or another target-typed expression. |
| <xref:lama0226> | A type, member, or expression combines run-time-only and compile-time-only elements. |
| <xref:lama0227> | A template uses dynamic as a generic argument, an array element type, a tuple element type, or a ref type. |
| <xref:lama0229> | A class that is both run-time and compile-time, such as an aspect, is nested in a run-time class. |
| <xref:lama0230> | A compile-time class nested in a run-time type, such as a type fabric, isn't private. |
| <xref:lama0231> | A compile-time type other than a type fabric is nested in a run-time type. |
| <xref:lama0232> | A template uses a C# feature that's newer than the C# version allowed in templates. |
| <xref:lama0233> | Compile-time code that isn't a template uses an API that's only allowed inside templates. |
| <xref:lama0235> | A template uses a type or member whose signature refers to a type that can't be resolved. |
| <xref:lama0236> | Code that can execute at compile time references a run-time-only declaration. |
| <xref:lama0237> | An abstract template property has a run-time-only type. |
| <xref:lama0238> | A member that isn't a template uses the dynamic type in a type that isn't run-time-only. |
| <xref:lama0241> | An expression in a template combines a compile-time sub-expression with a run-time sub-expression. |
| <xref:lama0242> | In a template, the type of an expression requires a different execution scope than its sub-expressions. |
| <xref:lama0244> | A type has a base type or interface whose execution scope is incompatible with its own. |
| <xref:lama0245> | A symbol combines run-time and compile-time elements in a way Metalama can't explain in detail. |
| <xref:lama0246> | A local function in a template uses dynamic in its signature. |
| <xref:lama0247> | A template returns a void expression where a value of another type is expected. |
| <xref:lama0248> | A compile-time declaration, such as an aspect class or a fabric, is marked as unsafe. |
| <xref:lama0249> | A template member is marked as unsafe. |
| <xref:lama0250> | A template uses dynamic in a cast, an is, as, or default expression, a lambda signature, or a method type argument. |
| <xref:lama0251> | A template initializes a dynamic local variable with an expression that isn't dynamic. |
| <xref:lama0252> | A template method, property, or indexer is declared as partial. |
| <xref:lama0253> | A template passes a value of a compile-time-only type to a run-time method. |
| <xref:lama0254> | The argument of ConfigureAwait after meta.ProceedAsync() isn't the literal true or false. |
| <xref:lama0255> | A template casts a run-time expression to a compile-time-only type. |
| <xref:lama0256> | A dynamic expression is passed to a compile-time method without an explicit cast to IExpression. |
| <xref:lama0257> | An aspect custom attribute sets a member of the aspect that is a template. |
| <xref:lama0258> | A finalizer, operator, conversion operator, or constructor is marked as a template. |
| <xref:lama0259> | The null-conditional operator mixes a compile-time receiver with a run-time member in a template. |
| <xref:lama0260> | A type fabric is nested in a compile-time or run-time-or-compile-time type. |
| <xref:lama0261> | A member has more than one template or advice attribute, such as both [Introduce] and [Template]. |
| <xref:lama0262> | A template or advice attribute is applied to an accessor instead of its property or event. |
| <xref:lama0263> | A lambda in a template has an expression body of type dynamic. |
| <xref:lama0264> | A compile-time template parameter has a type that exists only at run time. |
| <xref:lama0265> | A template accesses a static interface member through a compile-time type parameter. |
| <xref:lama0267> | A template converts an extension method to a delegate with a method group conversion. |
| <xref:lama0268> | Metalama can't resolve a template member, typically because of conflicting assembly references. |
| <xref:lama0269> | The same anonymous type is used in both run-time and compile-time code of a template. |
| <xref:lama0270> | A template calls an auxiliary template inside an expression instead of as a stand-alone statement. |
| <xref:lama0271> | A template method is declared as a C# extension method. |
| <xref:lama0272> | A void template contains a return statement that isn't needed. |
| <xref:lama0273> | A template references another template without calling it directly. |
| <xref:lama0274> | A template is declared in a type that isn't an aspect, a fabric, or a template provider. |
| <xref:lama0275> | A call to a virtual auxiliary template omits arguments of optional parameters. |
| <xref:lama0276> | A generic auxiliary template called from another template has a run-time type parameter. |
| <xref:lama0277> | A template passes a run-time type parameter as the type argument of a called template. |
| <xref:lama0278> | An aspect is declared as a struct instead of a class. |
| <xref:lama0279> | A template calls an auxiliary template that's abstract or empty. |
| <xref:lama0280> | A template sets a compile-time expression, such as a property of a compile-time object, in a block that depends on a run-time condition. |
| <xref:lama0281> | An attribute that wouldn't have the expected effect is applied to a compile-time declaration. |
| <xref:lama0282> | An aspect's template uses C# features that are newer than the C# version of the project where it's used. |
| <xref:lama0283> | A compile-time class or struct declares a primary constructor. |
| <xref:lama0284> | The scope of an anonymous method or of a lambda with a block body in a template can't be determined. |
| <xref:lama0285> | A local function declared in a template has a template or scope attribute. |
| <xref:lama0286> | A template casts a run-time expression that isn't dynamic to IExpression. |
| <xref:lama0287> | A template uses the receiver of the target member, but the member has no receiver. |
| <xref:lama0288> | A compile-time statement with side effects is in a block that depends on a run-time condition. |
| <xref:lama0289> | A template uses the ?. operator on a compile-time expression to access a run-time value. |
| <xref:lama0290> | Two versions of the same aspect library provide the same aspect type. |
| <xref:lama0291> | Code that isn't compile-time references a Roslyn type, which is compile-time-only in the project. |
| <xref:lama0292> | The scope of a member isn't compatible with the scope of its declaring type. |
| <xref:lama0293> | A template that wraps `meta.Proceed()` in a try-catch block can't override an async iterator method. |
| <xref:lama0294> | Compile-time code uses a C# feature, such as inline arrays, that .NET Standard 2.0 doesn't support. |
| <xref:lama0295> | Metalama can't find the declaration of a declarative advice member of an aspect, so the advice is ignored. |
